subject: general
question: Microfinance in India is a form of financial service which provides small loans and other financial services to poor and low-income households for ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**short term**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Microfinance** in India is a form of financial service which provides small loans and other financial services to poor and low-income households.
 
• These services are primarily aimed at providing **short-term** financial assistance, helping individuals to manage immediate needs and stabilize their economic conditions.
 
• Microfinance institutions (MFIs) offer a range of products including small loans, savings accounts, insurance, and remittance services.
 
• Loans provided by MFIs are typically of small amounts and have shorter repayment periods compared to traditional bank loans.
 
• The goal of microfinance is to promote financial inclusion and empower economically disadvantaged individuals by providing them with the necessary financial tools.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Microfinance has played a significant role in poverty alleviation by providing the poor with access to financial resources that were previously unavailable to them.
 
• The concept of microfinance gained global recognition through the work of **Dr. Muhammad Yunus** and the **Grameen Bank** in Bangladesh, which was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006.
 
• In India, microfinance has been supported by various policies and regulatory frameworks to ensure its sustainable growth and positive impact on society.
 
• Microfinance institutions must adhere to guidelines set by regulatory bodies such as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to ensure transparency and protect the interests of borrowers.
